Job Title: PA to Executive Director (Legal & Compliance Support)

Role Overview

Reporting to the Executive Director and supporting the Personal Assistant to the Group General Manager, the PA will provide structured legal support/ research, branch licensing/compliance assistance, premises search support, and on-site liaison for tenancy and renovation work. This is an execution-and-research role under clear management supervision—final legal opinions, contract decisions, and approvals remain with management or external counsel.

Key Responsibilities

1) Legal Compliance Support & Research (Under Management Supervision)

Conduct preliminary legal research on franchisee and education-related matters, including (but not limited to) the Human Resource Management, Education Ordinance, Employment Ordinance, and Occupiers’ Liability Ordinance for Hong Kong, mainland and overseas.

Review and flag key clauses in documents such as:

tenancy agreements

renovation contracts

service agreements

parent/student handbooks
(All final legal opinions remain with management and/or external counsel.)

Assist in preparing basic legal documents (e.g., license applications, statutory declarations) for management’s final review and signature.

Liaise with external lawyers when instructed (e.g., document delivery, meeting scheduling).

Monitor legislative/regulatory changes affecting private education institutions and provide summaries to the management team.

2) EDB Licensing & Compliance Support

Collect up-to-date licensing and compliance requirements from the Education Bureau and relevant authorities.

Complete application forms and compile submission documents (e.g., floor plans, fire safety records, etc.), and submit for management review and signature.

Track application progress and provide regular updates to the relevant team.

3) Premises Search & Initial Screening

Search for suitable rental units according to the Director’s criteria (e.g., size, budget, catchment area, zoning).

Conduct site visits to take basic evidence (e.g., photos) and record core data.

Prepare comparison tables to assist the Director’s decision-making.

No independent authority to shortlist final premises or sign any tenancy agreement.

4) Liaison for Tenancy & Renovation Works (Execution Support)

Tenancy: arrange site visits with agents, transmit required documents, and follow up on maintenance requests.

Renovation: accompany contractors on site, take measurements/photos, and relay simple instructions (as directed).

Compile communications, quotations, and draft documents, and submit them to management for final approval and signing.

5) Administrative & Field Support

Assist the Personal Assistant to the Group General Manager with HR support, scheduling, meeting minutes, and document preparation.

Perform field duties as assigned (e.g., document delivery, bank errands).

Requirements

Associate degree or above

1+ year experience in administration / legal support / project coordination

Demonstrable legal knowledge, such as:

diploma/degree in legal studies, or

paralegal certificate, or

relevant experience (e.g., contract review, regulatory research)

Knowledge of Hong Kong education / employment / tenancy-related laws is a strong advantage.

Ability to summarise legal information clearly for non-lawyer stakeholders.

Strong communication, documentation, and time-management skills.

Willingness to work on field duties are preferred.

Able to work on Saturdays and/ or Sundays

What We Offer

Clear boundaries and decision control:

You provide research and administrative/execution support.

Legal decisions, contract sign-offs, and policy approvals are made by your management team (or external counsel).

Stable work environment

With its unique “Liberal + Professional” education model, HSUHK nurtures young talent with critical thinking, innovative minds, caring attitudes, moral values and social responsibility.

Aspiring to be a leading private university in the region, HSUHK prioritises stellar undergraduate education, top-quality faculty members, award-winning green campus facilities, innovative degree programmes, a unique residential college system that combines living and learning, interactive small-class teaching, close student-teacher relationships, impactful research, and excellent student development and support services.

title: Corporate Communications & Fundraising Controller (Ref: BOD/CCFC)
snippet: We are looking for a high-calibre leader to integrate and oversee our Corporate Communications, Marketing, and Fundraising functions.
label: 翻译
full_jd:
About the Role

We are looking for a high-calibre leader to integrate and oversee our Corporate Communications, Marketing, and Fundraising functions. This strategic role requires an established professional with proven relationships with media leaders, corporate sponsors, and community partners. You will be instrumental in elevating Pok Oi’s brand profile while driving measurable revenue growth.

Key Success Factors

Strong PR background to enhance brand visibility – Proven experience in brand-building within an NGO institution (e.g., charity, healthcare, education). Deep media relations (print, TV, digital, news agencies) and strong working relationships with relevant government departments. Existing connections with decision-makers at charitable trusts and major corporate sponsors (e.g., banks, property developers, foundations).

Leverage multimedia & cross-platform channels – Track record of designing and executing multi-channel campaigns (social media, TV, SEO, physical events) that drive new corporate sponsorships or donation growth.

Strategy & team performance management – Experience developing and managing annual work plans for fundraising, communications, and marketing with clear KPIs to track sponsorship progress, media exposure, and fundraising ROI.  Target: increase net fundraising income by 10–15%.

Key Responsibilities:

Marketing Oversight

Lead multi-channel marketing strategies (digital, print, OOH, events) to drive brand awareness and sponsor engagement.

Oversee content production (videos, infographics, case studies, annual reports) to translate Pok Oi’s impact into compelling sponsor pitches.

Ensure monthly tracking and reporting of marketing metrics (reach, engagement, conversion).

Fundraising Oversight

Lead corporate, institutional, and major donor recruitment, retention, and management.

Leverage personal networks to engage C-suite executives, family offices, and foundation heads.

Set annual revenue targets and oversee grant applications, event fundraising, and online donation campaigns.

Corporate Communications Leadership

Act as Pok Oi’s brand guardian, ensuring message consistency across all external touchpoints.

Cultivate and maintain relationships with key media contacts (news editors, feature editors, broadcast producers) to secure positive coverage.

Lead crisis communications and reputation management.

Qualifications:

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Business Administration, Marketing, Public Relations, or a related field.

Minimum 15 years of relevant experience, with at least 8 years in senior management. Non-profit or related sector experience preferred.

Excellent written and spoken Chinese and English, capable of handling all communications settings.

Outstanding strategic planning, networking, and team leadership abilities.

Proven track record in successfully planning and executing large-scale brand promotion or fundraising campaigns with verifiable results.

Passion for social services, with a deep understanding of and commitment to Pok Oi Hospital’s mission and values.

The appointment will be made on a fixed-term contract basis. Interested candidates are invited to apply by sending full resume with current salary, expected salary and date available to Human Resources Controller, Pok Oi Hospital Board, UG/F., Pok Oi Hospital Jockey Club Care & Attention Home Building, Au Tau, Yuen Long or by email to hh•@pokoi.org.hk on or before 31 May 2026. Make recommendations to guests on appropriate wine choices on food and wine pairings

This position sits at the front line of defence, executing and monitoring security controls across endpoints, networks, privileged access, cloud environments, and software-as-a-service platforms to maintain a strong security posture across the organisation.

Working hands-on with incident response and emerging threat analysis, the role combines operational discipline with analytical thinking. Security requests are reviewed and approved with care, hygiene across the IT security footprint is maintained, and threat hunting techniques are applied to identify and respond to evolving risks. Collaboration is central, involving close engagement with business units, extended IT teams, external security operations centres, and third-party service providers.

Job rotation within IT security operations provides exposure to multiple domains and challenges, building depth and breadth in security expertise. Through investigation, forensics, audit support, and clear documentation, this role contributes directly to safeguarding the systems that keep Cathay moving people forward in life.
Key Responsibilities
• Execute and operate IT security solutions across endpoint, network, privileged access management, cloud, and software-as-a-service security platforms.

• Review and approve IT security requests in line with established policies and controls.

• Maintain strong security hygiene across the company’s IT network and systems.

• Perform basic threat hunting activities to identify and respond to emerging security threats.

• Investigate security incidents, including conducting incident response and forensic analysis.

• Collaborate with business units, extended IT teams, and external partners to address security challenges.

• Coordinate with third-party vendors and external security operations services to support incident response.

• Support audits by collecting evidence, updating documentation, and implementing recommended security controls.

• Develop and maintain documentation and assist in educating stakeholders on security events and their implications.

Requirements
• A minimum of 6 years of overall information technology experience, including at least 3 years of relevant IT security experience.

• Professional certifications such as Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP), Certified Information Security Manager (CISM), Certified in Risk and Information Systems Control (CRISC), ISO/IEC 27001 Lead Auditor, or equivalent experience are preferred.

• Demonstrated knowledge of IT security incident investigation and digital forensics.

• Strong understanding of compliance frameworks, including ISO/IEC 27001 and Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS).

• Proven ability to contribute to team development and provide coaching support.

• High level of self-motivation with a commitment to staying current with market standards and security technologies.

• A Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Cyber Security, or an equivalent discipline.

The Assistant Operations Manager supports the planning and execution of new lounge projects, working closely with senior management to coordinate design, fit‑out, vendor engagement, and operational readiness to ensure successful and timely launches in line with brand, safety, and operational standards.
In parallel, the role is responsible for assisting in the smooth day‑to‑day operations and effective management of business outlets during designated shifts. This includes supervising frontline teams, optimizing manpower deployment, and ensuring service efficiency, cost control, and profitability across all outlets.

What you will be doing: 
• (1) Daily Operation Management

• Oversee and monitor day‑to‑day lounge operations during designated shifts to ensure service quality and operational efficiency.

• Supervise frontline staff to ensure smooth, efficient, and profitable operations across lounges and business outlets.

• Ensure lounge set‑ups and product presentations comply with Company standards for quality, hygiene, safety, and aesthetics.

• Conduct regular inspections to maintain cleanliness, tidiness, safety, and proper functioning of facilities and equipment.

• Provide on‑the‑job coaching, guidance, and performance feedback to enhance team productivity and service standards.

• Organize and conduct briefing sessions to communicate operational updates, service changes, and service recovery learnings.

• Coordinate staff training, onboarding, and development to ensure service consistency and operational capability.

• Handle administrative duties including rostering, manpower planning, task assignments, attendance monitoring, and documentation.

• Act as on‑site lead for incident and emergency management, deploying reinforcement and implementing contingency measures.

• Handle guest enquiries, feedback, complaints, and external calls in a professional and timely manner.

• Ensure compliance with Company policies, operational procedures, safety regulations, and quality management system requirements.

• Identify operational gaps and improvement opportunities and participate in continuous improvement initiatives.

• Provide operational support and perform other duties as assigned by management.

•  
(2) New Project Management

• Support the planning and setup of new lounge projects to ensure operational readiness prior to opening.

• Coordinate with internal stakeholders, contractors, and vendors during project implementation.

• Assist in managing pre‑opening and post‑opening operational arrangements, including staffing deployment and workflow setup.

• Support service trials, readiness checks, and operational fine‑tuning for newly launched lounges.

What we are looking for: 
• Diploma or above in Hospitality Management, Business Administration, Operations Management, or related disciplines.

• Minimum six (6) years of relevant experience in hospitality, lounge operations, F&B, airline lounges, hotels, or other service‑based environments, with supervisory or leadership exposure.

• Proven experience in supervising frontline teams and supporting day‑to‑day operational management.

• Strong understanding of service quality standards, customer experience management, and operational procedures.

• Demonstrated experience in staff coaching, on‑the‑job training, performance management, and team development.

• Experience in staff rostering, manpower planning, task allocation, and general administrative duties.

• Hands‑on experience in handling operational incidents or emergency situations, with the ability to remain calm, decisive, and effective under pressure.

• Strong capability to manage guest enquiries, feedback, and complaints professionally, with a service‑recovery mindset.

• Experience or involvement in new outlet or lounge setup, pre‑opening preparation, or operational readiness is an advantage.

• Strong coordination and communication skills to work effectively with internal teams, vendors, and external stakeholders.

• High attention to detail, with the ability to uphold cleanliness, safety, facility functionality, and brand presentation standards.

• Knowledge of quality management systems, health and safety standards, and regulatory compliance is preferred.

• Proactive problem‑solving mindset, with the ability to identify improvement opportunities and support continuous improvement initiatives.

• Competent in basic computer applications (e.g. MS Word, Excel, Outlook) for reporting and administrative tasks.

• Good command of spoken and written English, Cantonese and Mandarin.

• Willingness to perform shift duties, including weekends and public holidays, as required by operational needs.

• Work location at various lounge facilities within airports or high‑speed railway stations.

About Kimpton Tsim Sha Tsui Hong Kong

Immerse yourself in a luxe metropolitan escape at Kimpton Tsim Sha Tsui Hong Kong, the city's 'culture of time' that intertwines modern interpretations of local heritage with multicultural cues. Our thoughtfully designed 495 rooms and suites are timeless, offering hidden luxuries like sunken bathtubs and cozy daybeds, all accompanied by captivating views of Victoria Harbour. We invite you to Kimpton Tsim Sha Tsui Hong Kong to embark on a unique journey of heartfelt connections and inspiring discoveries.

Why We’re Here

Kimpton believe heartfelt, human connections make people’s lives better. Especially the people who work here.

Our founder, Bill Kimpton rebelled against impersonal, genetic hospitality that makes people feel disconnected. He initiated a new boutique hotel standard and environment where people could connect, from the heart. That was the goal then, and it is still our purpose today.

Your work here has meaning. You’re here to improve the lives of coworkers, guests, owners, communities, and together we make that happen. It’s what drives all that we do. Every day you can improve lives in your own, unique way and you can expect the same in return. It all starts with you.

How We’re Different

Our San Francisco-born entrepreneurial spirit and zest for life kick started this culture in 1981, and it shines through to this day.

It all flows from you. The lively, rebellious, genuine you – with your diverse background, talents, experiences, and plucky personality – is fully welcome, and celebrated here. Because we know that when people can be themselves at work, they shine.

That’s what we seek out and celebrate. It’s people of all kinds who share a knack for creativity and self-leadership. People who don’t need to be told what to do to get things done. People who have an innate passion for making others’ lives better.

It adds up to a work environment that’s a bit quirky, irreverent, exciting, uncommon, empowering, and downright exceptional. Guess feel it; you’ll feel it too.

Looking to join a dynamic, prestigious, and reputable property agency in Hong Kong?
We are seeking driven, talented individuals like you to join our energy-packed team. We offer competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and unparalleled opportunities for career growth and development.

Join us in shaping the future of property in Hong Kong, where we set new standards of excellence in the industry. We are looking for those who are hardworking, driven, and passionate about innovation in real estate to be part of our team. If you're ready to propel your career to the next level, apply now, and become part of our dynamic and growing team!
Overview:
We are seeking a hands-on Assistant Marketing Manager who loves creating content as much as leading a team. In this role, you won't just oversee strategy; you will actively manage daily social media operations, craft compelling copy for Property & Mortgage topics, and work alongside your team to execute high-impact campaigns. If you enjoy "rolling up your sleeves" while mentoring junior staff, this is the place for you.
Key Responsibilities:
1. Hands-on Social Media Management
• Daily Execution: Take full ownership of the daily operation for Facebook, Instagram, Threads, and YouTube. This includes scheduling posts, community management (replying to comments), and ensuring content goes live on time.

• Content Production: Personally draft, edit, and polish engaging copy and multimedia content. You will be the "Chief Editor" ensuring every post meets our high standards for the Property & Mortgage sector.

• Platform Growth: actively monitor trends and adjust content tactics daily to maximize organic reach and engagement.

2. Team Supervision & Quality Control
• Operational Leadership: Lead the social media and campaign teams by example. Set clear daily/weekly tasks and provide direct feedback on their output.

• China Platform Oversight: Supervise the execution of China-focused platforms (XHS, WeChat, Douyin), ensuring the team delivers consistent and localized content.

3. Campaign Execution & Partnerships
• Implementation: Execute strategic partnerships and loyalty programs. You will be responsible for the logistical success of these campaigns, not just the planning.

• Performance Tracking: Monitor ad performance and SEO metrics, generating practical reports to fine-tune ongoing campaigns immediately.

4. Tech & Innovation
• AI Adoption: Actively utilize AI tools for copywriting efficiency and visual enhancement, teaching the team how to work smarter.

Job Requirements:
• Education: Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Marketing, Communications, Business Administration, or a related field.

• Experience: Minimum of 5 years in social media and digital marketing, including 1 year leading a team; experience in real estate or finance-related fields, or agency/new media background, is a plus.

• Language Skills: Proficient in Chinese and English, with excellent writing and storytelling abilities.

• Technical Skills: Experience in video editing, video production, and image editing is an advantage.

• Soft Skills: Highly creative, detail-oriented, and capable of managing multiple projects and teams in a fast-paced environment, with strong leadership and motivational abilities.

• Tech Savvy: Strong learning ability with familiarity in AI tools and marketing technologies.

• Candidates with less experience will be considered for the Supervisor position.

Interest parties please send your updated CV with current and expected salary by clicking “APPLY NOW” or go to our Company website at http://midland.com.hk. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. All personal data will be collected for recruitment purpose only and treated strictly confidential.

English Language Writer Duties of the English Language Writer will include – (1) preparing speeches and speaking points for senior officials; (2) writing press releases, advertorials, articles, op-eds, letters to the editors and social media posts; (3) producing content (including articles and video interviews) for major promotion projects and events; (4) copywriting for publicity materials; (5) editing work, such as newsletters, fact sheets, song sheets and contents produced by media partners; and (6) other English writing and editing duties (such as editorial and multimedia content production, quality control for online channels (including sourcing, scripting), and staff training). Assistant Editor (English) Duties of the Assistant Editor (English) will include – (1) vetting English content for news.gov.hk and its related social media platforms to ensure a high standard of English; (2) taking notes from major press conferences/briefings for preparing news stories and videos; (3) conducting interviews, including with government officials and sometimes expatriate interviewees, for preparing feature stories/videos; (4) editing voice-over scripts and narrating for news.gov.hk news and feature videos; (5) taking up other news.gov.hk editorial duties as assigned, such as developing story ideas and preparing Photo Galleries; (6) providing on-the-job training to other staff; and (7) other English writing and editing duties (such as press releases, speeches, transcripts, and publications).

Upon receipt of the on-line applications, ISD will send a separate email to applicants inviting them to indicate the post(s) they wish to apply for. As invitations and notifications will be issued via e-mail, applicants should provide an accurate e-mail address. Applicants are responsible for checking their e-mails to ensure that invitations and notifications will be duly received. Towards the application deadline, the on-line application system would likely be overloaded due to large volume of applications. To ensure timely completion of your on-line application, it is advisable to submit the application as early as possible. The following applications will not be considered: (a) late or incomplete applications; (b) applications submitted in person, by mail, fax, or email; (c) failure to provide the required information in the designated application form; (d) the information provided does not clearly demonstrate that the applicant meets the entry requirements; and (e) applications without replying to ISD’s email requesting indication of the post(s) being applied for. Applicants who are not invited to attend the written test within four months from the application closing date may assume their applications unsuccessful.__________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

title: Video Editor
label: 编辑
full_jd:
We are looking for a skilled and creative Video Editor to assemble recorded footage into high-quality finished videos for various platforms, including social media, websites and commercials. The ideal candidate will have a strong eye for detail, storytelling ability, and proficiency in video editing software.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities:
• Familiarise with the products and services, the target audience and their competitors’ activities.

• Edit raw footage into polished videos for social media, marketing campaigns, documentaries, commercials, and other projects.

• Trim, splice, and arrange video clips to create a compelling narrative.

• Add music, sound effects, voiceovers, graphics, animations, and subtitles to enhance video content.

• Colour correct and grade footage for a professional look.

• Ensure videos are edited, graded and produced to the branding demands.

• Optimise videos for different platforms (YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, TV, etc.).

• Amend, revise or redevelop adverts or campaigns in response to feedback from the creative director, account team or clients.

• Provide useful thoughtful and constructive contributions to team meetings and conversations.

• Develop creative ideas and concepts, often in partnership with other creative team members.

• Demonstrate strong project management skills: can take ownership of a task/project with excellent attention to detail.

• Maturity of thought and confidence to present and explain ideas to colleagues & management.

• Collaborate with other disciplines including production companies, photographers, designers, copywriters and printers.

• Ability to demonstrate excellence in creativity across multiple media.

Requirements:
• University degree or above in a relevant discipline and at least 2 years experience in equivalent role; or other qualifications plus 3+ years relevant experience.

• Proven experience as a Video Editor with a strong portfolio.

• Familiarity with different video formats, codecs, and export settings.

• Proficiency in video editing software (Adobe Premiere Pro, Final Cut Pro, DaVinci Resolve, After Effects, etc.).

• Knowledge of motion graphics, visual effects, and audio editing.

• Understanding of colour correction and grading techniques.

• Strong storytelling and pacing skills.

• Attention to detail and creative problem-solving abilities.

• Basic knowledge of camera equipment and filming techniques is a plus.

• Self-motivated, creative, independent, able to work under pressure and meet tight deadlines.

• Have a positive and passionate approach with a can-do attitude.

To apply, please submit your resume, cover letter, and expected salary by clicking Apply Now!

In line with CBRE’s global strategic focus on data superiority, CBRE is seeking an Asia Pacific Research Data Intelligence Manager capable of transforming commercial real estate data into information, insights and intelligence to inform business and client decision-making.

Transform commercial real estate data into information, insights and intelligence to inform business and client decision-making
Partner with global teams on project implementation, methodological alignment and data integrity

Extensive knowledge of data and analytics tools such as Power BI, SQL, Phyton, Power Query, DAX and familiar with mapping platform (e.g. Argis, Mapbox) integration with dashboards
Experience with generative AI technologies and application (such as prompt engineering, RAG, or Agentic AI) to drive process innovation and operational efficiency
Experience with API integration and ODBC connectors for extracting data from various sources will be highly advantageous
Experience with cloud platform (either Azure, AWS or GCP) or candidates with Power BI certificate (DA-100 or PL-300) will be highly advantageous
Project management skills with previous experience of managing projects from inception to finalisation
Fluency in written and spoken English, Cantonese, and Mandarin

url: https://www.recruit.com.hk/job-detail/easy-property-co-ltd/sales-management-trainee-見習分行經理-物業顧問-兼-職-物-業-顧-問/L0605951716
label: 管培生
full_jd:
機不可失！

不要看扁了地產代理從業員
在一般人印象中，物業代理是一個搵食艱難、為爭客時常大打出手及社會地位低微的職業，這其實是以偏概全的看法及美麗誤會：辣招打遏下，地產代理行業無疑大受打擊，但中長線而言，需要考牌的地產代理始終不失為一個專業和好行業；社會地位的高低及別人對你觀感的好壞，端看你的專業知識及專業操守是否足夠。我們十分有信心，憑著公司所提供的高水平培訓，有才幹的地產代理從業員完全可以以過人的專業知識和操守贏得崇高的社會地位。

怡居擁有九大優點:
 
• 歷史悠久，業績驕人 – 怡居專注經營沙田住宅已經39年，太古城35年，聲譽超著

• 經營的市場大而活躍 – 太古城及沙田每月的物業成交量成交價分別乃港島所有屋邨及新界各區之冠

• 實力過人 – 在王文彥先生領導下，怡居管理完善、架構完備、規制合理，才財兼備

• 盤多客多 – 三間分行雄據太古城及沙田優越位置，盤客俱多，做生意事半功倍

• 報酬特高 – 薪高佣厚，佣金分成尤其領先，以沙田為例，頭四萬元營業額，分佣較區內大行多60%，頭七萬元則多36%

• 資源最足 – 怡居不盲目擴充，屋邨內分行及營業員數目較少，營業員平均分配到的資源(特別是客源)因此最多

• 上位空間大 – 怡居乃仍在發展中的中型公司，許多好職位仍是等待著有才能的人坐上去，員工個人發展空間大

• 提供行內最高水平在職培訓 – 由王文彥先生親自策劃及主持培訓，水平行內最高

• 用升唯才 – 不用擦上司鞋，公司用人升人唯才，不講年資，不論嫡庶

• 上下和洽 – 絕無勾心鬥角之弊，自能提供愉快工作環境，充份發揮團隊精神

見習營業經理和物業顧問的前景：
 
• 怡居地產的最高領導人王文彥先生是中原地產兩位創辦人之一，至今仍擁有中原地產45%股權；

• 怡居地產並不缺乏資金，開100間分行都不成問題，它所缺乏的是一大群能征慣戰的將軍(分行經理)和士兵(物業顧問)。怡居分別招聘及培訓見習分行經理及物業顧問及將他們優化成為出色的分行經理及物業顧問就是要解決這個將才及精英不足的問題；

• 高素質的中層物業代理管理人材是目前本港勞動力市場很難提供的，故此我們寧願自己培訓，並期望將管理培訓班變成香港物業代理界的美國西點軍校。我們相信，所有完成管理培訓課程的畢業生會成為公司及業內管理精英，前程似錦；

•  怡居財、才兼備，有行內少見的巨大發潛力，你有多大的才能，怡居就可為你提供多大的發展舞台。今日是見習分行經理或物業顧問，將來卻可分別成為執行董事和區域經理；

• 怡居的報酬制度，遠勝大行和大多數中小行，有能力的員工，收入自是豐厚過人。

應徵條件：
 
• 應徵見習分行經理的，需具備良好思考及領導能力、勤奮、好學、積極、主動、進取，毋須地産經驗，但對地產和管理工作，有強烈興趣大學程度優先考慮。

• 應徵物業顧問的，擁有營業員牌照，勤奮、主動積極。

應徵兼職物業顧問的，必需：
•  擁有地產代理執業牌照

•  每星期工作6個上午 (9:30am至2:00pm) 或6個下午 (2:30pm至7:00pm)

You will manage sales pipelines, contract negotiations, marketing collateral, and client-specific quality protocols, ensuring our partners receive consistently graded, conflict-free polished diamonds that meet their design and compliance requirements.

Key Responsibilities:

Strategic Sales & Brand Account Management:

Serve as the primary internal point of contact for all sales and marketing matters related to polished diamonds, specifically regarding the 4Cs, certification standards (GIA/IGI), and parcel consistency required by luxury brand clients.
Develop and manage a detailed annual sales and marketing calendar aligned with diamond trading cycles, luxury fashion showrooms, and peak jewelry retail seasons (e.g., Chinese New Year, Q4 holidays).
Vet all client-specific MOQs, price bands, and quality tolerances during contract negotiation, paying special attention to diamond color and clarity grading, cut precision, and carat weight consistency across repeat orders.
Collaborate with the internal diamond sourcing and production teams to ensure rough or polished diamonds are allocated correctly for specific brand purchase orders (POs) and long-term supply agreements.
Oversee the timely issuance of all sales contracts, proforma invoices, and shipping documentation post-order confirmation, ensuring allocation to appropriate logistics partners based on value, destination, and insurance requirements.

Client Acquisition & Key Account Retention:

Ensure all brand client POs are acknowledged within 24–48 hours and confirmed with signed sales agreements outlining delivery schedules, certification requirements, and payment terms.
Monitor all active client orders and marketing initiatives weekly, ensuring sales targets and delivery timelines stay on track; proactively resolve bottlenecks in certification lead times, parcel sorting, or international shipping.
Ensure GIA/IGI certificate verification and diamond parcel integrity are maintained and transparently communicated to each client before shipment.
Liaise with third-party gemological labs and legal compliance officers to ensure all diamond parcels meet brand-specific ethical sourcing declarations (Kimberley Process, conflict-free guarantees, responsible sourcing reports).
Ensure brand trust and reputation are never compromised; relay any potential roadblocks such as grading discrepancies, supply shortages, or price volatility to senior management immediately with recommended mitigation strategies.
Create and submit invoices for all third-party non-product vendors (e.g., certification labs, secure logistics providers, insurance brokers, marketing agencies).

Brand Marketing & Industry Positioning:

Build and maintain long-term, trust-based relationships with procurement heads, design directors, and supply chain executives at major luxury jewelry houses and fashion brands.
Collaborate with the Sourcing Manager to adjust sales strategies based on market demand, pricing fluctuations in the polished diamond market, and emerging brand preferences (e.g., lab-grown vs. natural, traceability requirements).
Stay informed on Kimberley Process compliance, conflict-free diamond regulations, and emerging ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance) standards to ensure all marketing claims and client reports are legally compliant and competitive.
Partner with Product Development and Sourcing teams to ensure that client-specific grading requirements (e.g., “G+ color, VS clarity, excellent cut”) are technically feasible and consistently deliverable across large parcels.

Leadership & Cross-Functional Collaboration:

Build strong cross-functional partnerships with Sourcing, Logistics, Finance, and Compliance teams, intuitively knowing when to engage them to support client commitments and marketing campaign deliverables.
Manage up to senior leadership, keeping them informed of sales performance, market trends impacting polished diamond prices, competitive intelligence, and potential supply chain risks affecting client delivery promises.
Coordinate with the logistics team to ensure smooth international shipping, customs clearance, and insurance coverage for high-value polished diamond parcels destined for brand clients in key markets (e.g., Greater China, Europe, North America).

Qualifications & Requirements:

Experience: 4+ years of experience in B2B sales management, key account management, or marketing within the polished diamond trading, diamond manufacturing, or fine jewelry wholesale industry at a managerial level is a MUST.
Industry Knowledge: Deep, verifiable understanding of the 4Cs (Cut, Color, Clarity, Carat), GIA/IGI certification standards, polished diamond pricing matrices, and the specific quality requirements of high-end jewelry brands is a MUST.
Technical Skills: Proficiency in CRM software (e.g., Salesforce, Zoho), inventory-linked sales platforms, and diamond grading report verification tools. Experience with RapNet, IDEX, or Jewelry ERP is a plus.
Client Network: Established network of procurement decision-makers at large luxury jewelry retailers, international fashion houses, or high-volume diamond buyers is highly desirable.
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Marketing, Gemology (GIA Graduate Gemologist or equivalent), or a related field.

HONG KONG CHU HAI COLLEGE

 

Chu Hai College has provided 78 years of quality education and excellence to the Hong Kong community and remains committed to enhancing educational opportunities for young people. Its purpose and vision are to nurture future leaders, strengthen the competitiveness of Hong Kong, and help bring about a stable, prosperous and harmonious society in a knowledge-based economy.

 

Academic departments within the College include Chinese Literature, English, Journalism and Communication, Business Administration, Accounting and Banking, Finance, Computer Science, Civil Engineering, and Architecture. The Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences consists of three Departments and offers innovative curricula that respond to the needs of society and equip students to become employable graduates and responsible citizens with lifelong learning.

 

The College is registered as an Approved Post Secondary College under the Post-Secondary Colleges Ordinance (Cap 320), with all degree programmes accredited by the Hong Kong Council for Accreditation of Academic and Vocational Qualifications (HKCAAVQ).

 

The Dean of Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences is responsible for providing overall effective leadership in the management and development of the Faculty, the development of appropriate programmes in response to community needs, the smooth operation of programmes, the conduct of good quality teaching and learning activities, the promotion of research and scholarship and the establishment of partnerships with various external stakeholders in the Government, the academic profession and the industry.

Lingnan University is one of the eight publicly funded institutions in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) of the People’s Republic of China (PRC) and has the longest established tradition among the local institutions of higher education. It is widely recognised for providing quality education with a focus on whole-person development and conducting high-impact research for a better world. Moving forward, Lingnan University is well positioned to take lead as a comprehensive university in arts and sciences in the digital era, with impactful research and innovations.

Lingnan University offers undergraduate, taught postgraduate, and research postgraduate programmes in the Faculties of Arts, Business, Social Sciences, and the Schools of Data Science, Graduate Studies and Interdisciplinary Studies. To foster interdisciplinary collaboration and scientific progress, Lingnan University established the Lingnan University Institute for Advanced Study (LUIAS), attracting distinguished scholars from around the world to collaborate with its faculty and students. With traditional strengths in arts, business, social sciences, and interdisciplinary studies, the University aims to equip students with practical knowledge and critical thinking skills to thrive in the future. Subsequent to the establishment of the School of Data Science and LUIAS, Lingnan University is transforming into a hub for global leaders to develop and promote human-centric technology and social policies. Further information about Lingnan University is available at https://www.ln.edu.hk/.

full_jd:
About the Role

FundPark is on the lookout for a strategic, visionary, and hands-on Head of Brand & Content to supercharge our brand storytelling, elevate our communications presence, and drive consistent, scalable creative excellence across our organization. You will take the lead in unifying our brand voice, shaping bold and effective communication strategies, and creating compelling narratives that build affinity with our growing ecosystem of fintech partners, SMEs, investors, and talent.

This high-impact role is perfect for an ambitious, action-oriented leader who’s excited about both strategy and execution — driving centralised, cross-functional creative and content operations from ideation to delivery. You’ll oversee branding, corporate comms, PR, and content—infused with innovation, technology, and AI-led tools to keep us ahead of the curve.

What You’ll Do

Own FundPark’s brand strategy end-to-end: define, evolve, and scale a bold, consistent brand across markets and channels.

Act as FundPark’s brand guardian, ensuring a consistent tone of voice, look & feel, and messaging across all communications—while inspiring internal storytelling and alignment.

Develop and execute thought leadership and PR strategies to build awareness and trust among stakeholders and media partners.

Lead and centralise content creation for marketing, PR, investor comms, and internal messaging—ensuring quality, scalability, and differentiation.

Work cross-functionally with marketing, product, HR, legal, and executive teams to deliver strategic content that drives FundPark’s growth goals.

Lead and manage relationships with creative, PR, and media agencies, ensuring best-in-class external production and delivery.

Incorporate data insights, AI tools, and the latest innovation into daily content operations to increase performance, productivity and personalisation.

Oversee corporate events and sponsorship communications, ensuring cohesive branding, messaging, and post-event amplification.

Build, mentor, and lead a high-performing brand and content team, fostering creativity, accountability, and collaboration.

Measure impact across all brand and content investments—track KPIs and insights to improve content effectiveness and business value.

What We’re Looking For

Minimum 10+ years of experience in brand, content, marketing communications, or PR—ideally across high-growth companies or creative agencies.

Proven leadership and cross-functional collaboration ability, with experience running content teams or brand functions across multiple stakeholders.

Experience in working with external vendors/agencies to produce high-quality, on-brand creative and communication assets.

Bilingual proficiency in Chinese (Cantonese/Mandarin) and English is a must—spoken and written.

Experience building strategic brand and content frameworks that scale across regions and channels.

Part-time Research Assistant, School of Computing and Information Sciences
(Ref.: 26/66/CIS/RA)

Join an innovative, high-impact research initiative at St. Francis University. The project, "AI and IoT Monitoring of Construction Tower Cranes," focuses on enhancing smart city infrastructure and construction safety. By integrating Internet of Things (IoT) sensors with advanced Artificial Intelligence (AI), this project aims to enable real-time structural health monitoring, predictive maintenance, and anomaly detection for tower cranes on active construction sites.

We are seeking a technically skilled, motivated Part-Time Research Assistant (RA) with an engineering background. In this role, you will help bridge the gap between structural/mechanical systems and intelligent data science, contributing directly to the deployment of IoT hardware and the development of AI algorithms.

Duties:

Develop, train, and test AI/Machine Learning models for anomaly detection and predictive analytics using sensor data.

Assist in processing, cleaning, and managing time-series data streams from IoT sensors (e.g., accelerometers, strain gauges, tilt sensors).

Support the configuration, calibration, and data acquisition setup for IoT monitoring hardware.

Collaborate with the research team to validate AI model insights against real-world engineering constraints.

Assist in preparing technical reports, progress updates, and academic publications.

Appointment Criteria

A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree (or currently enrolled in a postgraduate program) in Engineering (e.g., Civil, Mechanical, Electronic, Systems, or Biomedical Engineering with a strong structural/mechatronics focus).

Strong programming skills in Python or MATLAB (experience with libraries like NumPy, Pandas, TensorFlow, or PyTorch is highly preferred).

Solid understanding of Machine Learning, Deep Learning, or statistical signal processing.

Ability to interpret data related to structural mechanics, vibrations, or kinematics.

Experience working with IoT hardware, microcontrollers (e.g., Arduino, Raspberry Pi), or edge computing.

Strong problem-solving abilities and a self-driven attitude toward research.

Good written and verbal communication skills.

Salary will be commensurate with qualifications and experience. Interested parties are invited to submit (i) an application letter indicating expected salary; (ii) an updated CV; and (iii) a duly completed application form (obtainable at University’s career site), by email at hr•@sfu.edu.hk. (b) have met the language proficiency requirements of Level 2 [see Note (1)] or above in Chinese Language and English Language in the Hong Kong Diploma of Secondary Education Examination or the Hong Kong Certificate of Education Examination (HKCEE), or equivalent; and
(c) be able to speak fluent Cantonese.
Note: (1) For non-civil service appointment purpose, “Grade E” in Chinese Language and English Language (Syllabus B) in previous HKCEE before 2007 is accepted administratively as comparable to “Level 2” in Chinese Language and English Language in the 2007 HKCEE and henceforth.
Duties: An Assistant Music Officer II (Chinese) is mainly deployed to:
(a) teach instrumental training classes and to liaise with parents on matters relating to the classes; to carry out administrative duties pertaining to his/her teaching jobs and to assist in recruitment of instrumental classes trainees;
(b) serve as member of the concurrent recruitment panels for the Instrumental Music Training Scheme classes, orchestra/band audition boards, Music Camp recruitment panels, and Internal Assessment panels;
(c) prepare teaching materials and select repertoire for instrumental training classes under his/her charge;
(d) serve as tutti player in the Instructor’s Orchestra/Ensemble;
(e) serve as the conductor of elementary and/or intermediate level orchestras/bands and to assist in their training, management and operation;
(f) assist in administrative matters concerning recruitment and audition of band and orchestra members; and
(g) assist in monitoring the maintenance and minor repair of musical instruments and in making evaluation and procurement recommendations, and to assist in checking of instruments upon procurement.

(Note: May be required to work irregular hours.)
Terms of Appointment: Successful candidates will be appointed on non-civil service contract terms for a period of one year.
General Notes: (a) Candidates must be permanent residents of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region at the time of appointment unless specified otherwise.
(b) As an Equal Opportunities Employer, the Government is committed to eliminating discrimination in employment. The vacancy advertised is open to all applicants meeting the basic entry requirement irrespective of their disability, sex, marital status, pregnancy, age, family status, sexual orientation and race.
(c) Non-civil service vacancies are not posts on the civil service establishment. Candidates appointed are not on civil service terms of appointment and conditions of service. Candidates appointed are not civil servants and will not be eligible for posting, promotion or transfer to any posts in the Civil Service.
(d) The entry pay, terms of appointment and conditions of service to be offered are subject to the provisions prevailing at the time the offer of appointment is made.
(e) Where a large number of candidates meet the specified entry requirements, the recruiting department may devise shortlisting criteria to select the better qualified candidates for further processing. In these circumstances, only shortlisted candidates will be invited to attend recruitment examination and/or interview.
(f) It is Government policy to place people with a disability in appropriate jobs wherever possible. If a disabled candidate meets the entry requirements, he/she will be invited to attend the selection interview/written examination without being subject to any further shortlisting criteria. Applicants who have declared disabilities found suitable for appointment may be given an appropriate degree of preference over other applicants whose suitability for appointment is considered comparable to that of the former. The Government policy and other related measures on employment of persons with disabilities are set out in the booklet “Employ People Based on Their Abilities – Application for Government Jobs by Persons with Disabilities” which is available for reference on the Civil Service Bureau's website at https://www.csb.gov.hk under “Administration of the Civil Service – Appointments”.
(g) Holders of academic qualifications other than those obtained from Hong Kong institutions/Hong Kong Examinations and Assessment Authority may also apply but their qualifications will be subject to assessments on equivalence with the required entry qualifications. They should submit all copies of their official transcripts of studies and certificates by email to eomopg@lcsd.gov.hk on or before 4 June 2026. Candidates should mark the post applied for and quote the on-line application number on the copies of every page of supporting documents.
(h) Towards the application deadline, our online system would likely be overloaded due to large volume of applications. To ensure timely completion of your online application, it is advisable to submit the application as early as possible.
How to apply: Applicants must apply online through the G.F. 340 Online Application System of the Civil Service Bureau (https://www.csb.gov.hk) on or before 4 June 2026. Candidates should state clearly in their applications full record of employment, academic qualifications (including the major instrument(s) for which the relevant diploma / associate diploma was awarded) and Chinese and English languages proficiency level as shortlisting criteria may be applied for selecting better qualified candidates to audition and selection interview. Applications which are incomplete or submitted in person, by post, by fax or by e-mail will not be accepted.

Over the years we have established a feeder system (including selection and training) with most of the national sports associations (NSAs).  It provides our student athletes the quality training required for them to achieve higher performance in the All China Secondary School Students Games, inter-port and other international competitions.  In addition, those potential athletes will be able to feed to the NSAs, to prepare them for higher level of competitions in future.

Mizuho has a long-term commitment to the Hong Kong market. Our clients primarily comprise Japanese and non-Japanese corporations (including those domiciled in the PRC), financial institutions, and government and quasi-government organizations. Why Mizuho

At Mizuho, we provide the stability of an international industry leader with the career trajectory of a growing business. Our steady, strategic growth gives our people at all levels rewarding degrees of responsibility and a richer work experience than a boutique firm or an established giant could offer alone.

About the team

Loan Operations Section is responsible for executing bilateral loans and syndicated loans drawdown, rollover and repayment and the related booking. It also ensures the loan conditions are met and properly registered before execution. Moreover, it processes the agency loan operations and settlements which include execution of drawdown, rollover and repayment, confirmation and notification of drawdown, interest due and rate fixing to the borrowers and the syndicated loan participants.

The Syndication Loan Team is responsible for managing the daily demanding and more complexed Syndication Loan transactions. The team is required to support LOP to handle system projects initiated by Head Office.

Role requirements

To process and check the booking and settlement of the operations handled by the Section, for bilateral / syndicated / agent loans and guarantee issuance, etc.
To arrange for necessary fund disbursements, etc.;
To alert superiors of operation and control deficiencies;
To prepare relevant reports required by superiors, the Management, Head Office and the regulators within deadline;
To answer the general enquiries of internal and external parties in relation to the Section’s operations;
To prepare, review and check loan agreements, loan confirmations, audit confirmations, balance certificates, etc.;
To observe and comply with all the established operation / procedure manuals and guidelines;
To provide inputs to the re-engineering and enhancement projects for operations, control and IT enhancement;
To perform other general administration duties for the Section.

Essential Functions

Support Loan Operations Section to conduct the daily operations, solve issues, promote customer satisfaction and perform all other administrative tasks in order to be in line with management's directions and comply with H.O. and local regulatory requirements.

Competencies

We are looking for an individual who has mind-set to make improvements for higher productivity and performance;
Continuously acquiring necessary knowledge through day to day work and training, the individual should learn to work independently or in a team;
The individual respects for and commits to high standards of business conduct and integrity in conducting operations, reporting and etc.

Bachelor’s Degree;
1-2 years of experience in handling Syndication or Agency Loans administration;
A team player, agility to learn and attention to details;
Fluency in English, Cantonese, and Mandarin an advantage;
Proficiency in MS Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.

f. Participate in internal discussions and knowledge sharing to enhance the team’s research capabilities.

a.Master’s degree or above in Finance, Economics, Accounting, Mathematics or related STEM fields is preferred.

b.Minimum 3 years of relevant work experience; buy-side research experience is a plus;
c. Solid understanding of financial statements and valuation methodologies (DCF, comparable company analysis, etc.);
d. Basic knowledge of Hong Kong and US stock markets, with awareness of industry trends and market dynamics;
e. Proficiency in Bloomberg, Wind, Excel; experience with Python/SQL is a plus;
f. Language proficiency: Fluent in Mandarin and English; Cantonese is an asset;
g. Strong logical thinking, independent reasoning, and teamwork skills; high sense of responsibility and ability to work under pressure.

We Offer
a. Competitive compensation package (fixed salary + performance-based bonus);
b. Flat organizational structure, working closely with experienced investment professionals for rapid growth;
c. Opportunity to systematically learn professional investment research and portfolio management within a licensed Family Office;
d. Clear career progression path supporting long-term development in research.

職位概述
我們正在尋找數位具備紮實研究能力、對企業分析有濃厚熱情且邏輯清晰的個股研究員，加入我們的投資團隊。您將專注於港股或美股上市公司研究，深入分析企業基本面、行業趨勢與估值水平，為投資決策提供數據支持與投資建議。此職位適合有志於在家族辦公室環境中深耕個股研究、並與投資團隊緊密協作的專業人士。

主要職責
a. 深入研究覆蓋的港股或美股上市公司，進行財務分析、估值建模、行業比較與投資價值評估；
b. 跟蹤覆蓋公司的業務動態、財報發布、管理層變動及市場情緒變化；
c. 撰寫個股研究報告，提出明確的投資建議與風險提示；
d. 維護並更新個股研究數據庫，支持投資組合的構建與調整；
e. 協助資深投資經理進行專題研究、策略回測及市場監測；
f. 參與內部分享與討論，提升團隊整體研究深度與廣度。

任職要求

a. 碩士或以上學歷，金融、經濟、會計、數學或相關理工科專業優先；

b. 具備3年以上相關工作經驗，有買方研究經驗者更佳；
c. 具備紮實的財務分析基礎與估值建模能力，熟悉財務報表解讀與DCF、可比公司分析等方法；
d. 對港股或美股市場有基本認識，關注行業趨勢與市場動態；
e. 熟練使用Bloomberg、Wind、Excel等工具，有Python/SQL能力者優先；
f. 語言要求：流利普通話及英語，粵語為優勢；
g. 具備優秀的邏輯思維能力、獨立思考能力與團隊協作精神，責任心強，抗壓能力佳。

我們提供
a. 具競爭力的薪酬組合（固定薪金 + 績效獎金）；
b. 扁平化管理，直接與資深投資團隊合作，快速成長；
c. 在持牌家族辦公室內系統學習專業投資研究與組合管理的機會；
d. 清晰的職業發展路徑，支持長期投研方向深耕。

About the Team

At GreenPrice, sustainability is at the heart of everything we do. High-quality but short-dated food products often go straight from the shelves to the landfills. We are on a mission to further the lifecycle of these products by redirecting them to homes at half-price or less. Our social enterprise operates 18 stores, collaborates with thousands of inspired international brands and places technology at the heart of our activities. In the past year, we have witnessed remarkable growth in our online business, while successfully expanding our sourcing network to France and the UK. These achievements have not gone unnoticed, as our dedicated team was honoured with the B Corp certification and Forbes 30 Under 30 2023 award. We’re quickly growing the team, come & meet us!

Our Buying team is ultimately responsible for the products we sell. While most retail buyers only go out a few times a year, ours are always out saving amazing products at the verge of disposal. You will be introduced to buying and given the chance to gain invaluable experience, analysing and identifying business trends while reporting directly to an experienced Purchasing Lead. After sufficient training, you will start using your negotiation skills to make buying decisions on the spot. This means you can stay very close to the business and be more flexible – as well as negotiate some fantastic deals. You will be an entrepreneur, have the responsibility and make a big impact. We offer a really exciting career path for a long-term future.

title: Organization Development Manager (Full-time/ Part-time)
snippet: Be Priceless is a health education non-profit improving diverse children and families' well-being, safety, and togetherness. www.bepriceless.org
location: Cheung Sha Wan ·  Sham Shui Po District
label: 项目
full_jd:
Be Priceless is a health educational non-profit with the mission to enhance child protection, well-being, personal growth, and supportive relationships - especially disadvantaged children (SEN, ethnically diverse, low-income, single parent, and crisis affected families) We foster health behaviours of children, youth, and caregivers through SEED health education, community partnerships and participatory research. Our vision is that all children are rooted in a flourishing foundation of health, nurtured by their families, schools and communities. 

Our team is trans-sectoral, including doctor, educator, social worker, counsellor, and more. We are passionate about nurturing the flourishing and health equity of our diverse community. We are looking for a new Head of Development or COO, who will lead the development of our organization into implementing our strategy that will empower 50,000 children and caregivers by 2035 - that is 1 in 15 children living in poverty across HK to have improved health, well-being, safety, and relationships that lasts across their childhood. Are you interested and suitable? 

What you’ll be doing?

In this role, you will be a leading our organization's fundraising, branding, business and operational development, including managing our trans-sectoral professional team. You will have abundant opportunities for personal and professional development. 

You will explore and develop resources to support our programs of community services. This includes establishing donations, revenue generation, and donors management systems. This also includes building strong positive branding, trust and relationships with funders, partners, and community members.

You will play a key role in developing our contribution to the system change for vulnerable children to grow up with personal, family, community, and environmental health and safety. You will drive the implementation of our strategy both internally in our organization and externally with diverse trans-sectoral collaborators - including funders, corporates, government departments, community groups, and more. The goal is to cultivate sustainable systems change to exponentiate our transformative impact for children's safety, health, and safety net. 

Who are we looking for? (Requirements)

6+ years strong professional experience and track record in fundraising and management for a non-profit organization

The following experience would be an advantage:

Organizational development, organizational psychology, human resources, systems building, non-profit or business management.

Designing and implementing successful organizational development initiatives

Excellent self-mastery, including emotional regulation, time management, positive communications, and high standards for work performance

Good interpersonal and communication skills with growth mindset 

Excellent language skills in English and Chinese, verbal and written

Excellent interpersonal and communication skills with ability to foster strong support from corporates, schools, donors, and others. 

Our team takes integrity very seriously. We have strong policies and protocols for ensuring child safety, data security, and other risk management. All staff must undergo regular background checks [including previous employment checks and Sexual Conviction Records Check (SCRC)] and abide by the Be Priceless code of conduct including for strict child safeguarding and data security policies are requirements. We have continuous and rigorous monitoring of issues of concerns safety of children and other vulnerable individuals. We will investigate/ report where appropriate. 

Details:

Full time, 5 days work week

Compensation off for overtime (e.g. for 1.5x CO for weekend work)

Health insurance  

Annual leave for 20 days (full time)

Why you should consider this opportunity:
We offer an attractive remuneration package with benefits to the right candidate, such as

COO, Head of Development - Fundraising, business and operations development

Permanent role, compensated overtime, generous leave

Performance bonus every season (for excellence, integrity, and commitment)

Mentoring and professional development opportunities,  e.g. behavioral change, data-driven decision making, impact assessments, compassionate systems change

Empowering team culture that is positive, collaborative, and mission-committed

Impact fully improve vulnerable children's safety & well-being

Work in an multi-award wining team with deep trans-sectoral expertise

If you wish to join us to improve vulnerable children's well-being and you have the right expertise as well as a passion for nurturing a healthy community, please apply now by submitting your 1) cover letter and 2) resume to us. Please include information about your professional purpose or passion, how that aligns with Be Priceless' purpose, your relevant experience and values, working languages, expected salary, and date of availability. 

We look forward to hearing from you.

All information received will be kept in strict confidence and will be treated only for employment-related purposes.

snippet:
CUHK Business School
Project Co-ordinator II, Student Learning & Development, Office of MBA Programme in Finance
label: 项目
full_jd:
CUHK Business School
Project Co-ordinator II, Student Learning & Development, Office of MBA Programme in Finance (Ref. 260000UQ) (Closing date: June 5, 2026)

 

The CUHK Business School is a leading business school and a pioneer in business education in Hong Kong. Since its establishment in Hong Kong in 1963, the CUHK Business School has gained world recognition of nurturing business leaders with immense contributions in the Asia Pacific. The School has been offering a comprehensive range of undergraduate and postgraduate programmes with over 5,000 students from 30+ countries/regions, as well as executive education. It has one of the most extensive alumni networks in the region, with over 47,000 alumni around the world.

 

Among all the Master’s programmes offered by the School, the MBA Programme in Finance (FMBA) stands out as a highly selective programme designed to attract highly motivated professionals in the financial and related business sectors. This part-time programme caters to the needs of working professionals in Hong Kong, Chinese Mainland and the region who seek leadership development. To support the strategic development, the School is looking for an experienced Project Co-ordinator II for the FMBA Programme.

 

Reporting to the Head of the Student Learning & Development, FMBA Programme, the appointee will be responsible for (a) assisting in end-to-end course management, including course planning and timetabling, preparation of course and teaching materials, as well as coordination and communication on course scheduling with faculty, students and relevant departments; (b) undertaking general administrative duties to support the Executive Officer, including: handling all correspondence and communications with staff and students, organising meetings, room booking, maintaining and updating databases, arranging transportation, accommodation, and catering as required to support programme delivery; (c) organising and providing logistical support to the Programme-related events and activities, including orientation, graduation, study trips and related student and alumni activities; (d) providing excellent student service and building good relationships with alumni and prospective students; and (e) performing other ad-hoc duties as assigned. Traveling to the Chinese Mainland and work outside normal office hours will be required occasionally.

 

Applicants should have (i) a Bachelor’s degree; (ii) at least 2 years’ full-time work experience; (iii) self-motivation with a strong sense of commitment; (iv) the ability to work effectively as a good team member; (v) an excellent command of both written and spoken English and Chinese (including fluency in Putonghua); and (vi) the ability to work independently. Shortlisted candidates may be invited for interviews and / or written test(s), as appropriate.

 

Applicants must submit copies of certificates showing that they have fulfilled the academic qualifications stated above, otherwise their applications will NOT be considered.

 

Appointment will initially be made on a 2-year contract with contract-end gratuity, renewable subject to good performance and mutual agreement.

 

[CUHK Business School is also known as the Faculty of Business Administration.]

 

The University only accepts and considers applications submitted online for the post above via the CUHK career site. For more information and to apply online, please visit http://career.cuhk.edu.hk.

CUHK Business School
Executive Officer II / Project Co-ordinator II (carrying the job title of ‘Corporate Outreach and Career Advisory Manager / Corporate Outreach and Career Advisory Assistant Manager’), Career Development and Corporate Engagement Office (Ref. 260000UR) (Closing date: June 5, 2026)

The CUHK Business School is a leading business school and a pioneer in business education in Hong Kong. Since its establishment in Hong Kong in 1963, the CUHK Business School has gained world recognition of nurturing business leaders with immense contributions in the Asia Pacific. The School has been offering a comprehensive range of undergraduate and postgraduate programmes with over 5,000 students from 30+ countries/regions, as well as executive education. It has one of the most extensive alumni networks in the region, with over 47,000 alumni around the world.

 

The Career Development and Corporate Engagement Office (CDCEO) spearheads corporate partnerships and academic-industry collaboration. This role is pivotal in bridging the school’s academic excellence with regional industry needs, driving employability initiatives, and securing strategic opportunities for students and faculty. Candidates with a background in regional business development, sales, or in recruitment positions are strongly preferred.

 

Reporting to the Senior Manager of the CDCEO, the appointee will be responsible for (a) serving as the primary liaison between the Business School and corporations, institutions, associations across Hong Kong, Greater Bay Area, and Asia-Pacific; (b) developing and executing strategies to secure partnerships, particularly within Chinese Mainland, for student internships and recruitment programs; (c) partnering with colleagues on events planning, marketing and communication; (d) negotiating and formalizing MOUs, sponsorships, and collaborative agreements aligned with the school’s academic priorities and employability initiatives; (e) representing the school at industry events, conferences, and corporate meetings to amplify visibility and foster long-term relationships; (f) tracking graduate employment outcomes and leveraging data to refine corporate engagement strategies in the Chinese Mainland market; and (g) assisting in ad-hoc career projects and any other duties as assigned. Working at flexible hours and travelling will be required.

 

Applicants should have (i) a Bachelor’s degree, preferably a Master’s degree; (ii) fulfilled the English Language requirement set on the website: https://www.hro.cuhk.edu.hk/en-gb/languageforeo (for Executive Officer II, carrying the job title of ‘Corporate Outreach and Career Advisory Manager’); (iii) at least 8 years of post-qualification executive and professional experience in business development, client management, or in recruitment positions; (iv) an excellent command of written and spoken English and Chinese (including fluency in Putonghua); and (v) a track record in corporate relations, preferably with established networks in the Chinese Mainland. Having knowledge of career management and Chinese Mainland market dynamics will be an advantage. Applicants with less experience will be considered for appointment as Project Co-ordinator II (carrying the job title of ‘Corporate Outreach and Career Advisory Assistant Manager’). Shortlisted candidates may be invited for interviews and to sit for a written test.

 

Applicants must submit copies of certificates showing that they have fulfilled the language requirements and academic qualifications stated above, otherwise their applications will NOT be considered.

 

Appointment will initially be made on a 2-year contract with contract-end gratuity commencing as soon as possible, renewable subject to good performance and mutual agreement.

 

[CUHK Business School is also known as the Faculty of Business Administration.]

 

The University only accepts and considers applications submitted online for the post above via the CUHK career site. For more information and to apply online, please visit http://career.cuhk.edu.hk.

title: Experience Manager at Single Family Office
snippet: A role for someone with the taste to plan the unforgettable, the judgement to be trusted with it, and the operating skill to actually pull it off.
label: 市场
full_jd:
A Hong Kong based single family office is looking for an Experience Manager to run personal events, gifting, lifestyle logistics, and household operations for the principal. You'll work directly with the principal and own this side of the office.

A role for someone with the taste to plan the unforgettable, the judgement to be trusted with it, and the operating skill to actually pull it off.

https://theexperiencerole.com/

A complete remit

01

A handful of personal events each year for the principal. Anniversaries, birthdays, milestone celebrations. Guest counts range from intimate dinners for two to small gatherings of up to twenty, across Asia, the Americas, Europe, and Oceania. You take the brief, scout the venues, book private jets, charter yachts, and secure castles. You manage the vendors, the budget, and you are there on the ground for the moments that matter.

02

Gifting for a defined circle of family and close friends. You run the program end to end, including the institutional memory behind it.

03

Oversight of a small household team including captains, drivers, and domestic staff. Hiring (you screen and recommend, principal decides), scheduling, and performance.

04

Asset administration across the family's vehicles and yacht. Licenses, insurance, registrations, surveys, and renewals all sit with you, working with the relevant brokers and external providers.

05

Administration of an international real estate portfolio including a private island. Property managers, caretakers, renovation projects, insurance, utilities, taxes, and access logistics across multiple jurisdictions. You coordinate the people on the ground at each location and keep every property guest-ready.

06

Hiring other personal vendors as needed. Trainers, tutors, photographers, household staff for extended family. You interview, recommend, and onboard once the principal signs off.

Taste over spend

Budget is meaningful but it isn't the point. We're looking for someone who pulls off miracles with creativity and taste, not by throwing money at the problem. The most memorable moments aren't always the most expensive ones, and we want someone who knows the difference.

Where this takes you

This role does not live behind a desk. You will be on the ground at a villa on Lake Como in spring. The South Island of New Zealand in summer. The Arctic Circle in autumn for the northern lights. A schloss in the Salzkammergut for a winter dinner.

You will arrange the private jets that bring the principal's guests in. You will charter sailing yachts in the Mediterranean and the Whitsundays. You will arrange a private excursion to Antarctica. You will scout palazzi in Venice and finca-style retreats in Mallorca months before the rest of the world knows them. You will know the chef who closes the restaurant for one table, the property manager who answers the phone at 4am, the pilot who lands on the glacier strip.

You work behind the scenes. The guests should never see the choreography, only the experience. You will spend time in some of the most beautiful places on earth.

The person we're looking for

Five or more years in luxury hospitality events, private members clubs, family office, bespoke event planning, or private client services at an auction house. Experience managing household or crew staff is a strong plus.

Strong English. Cantonese a plus. You're a self-starter who can brief a vendor cold and make calls without running every detail past the principal.

Privacy matters in this household and we expect it from whoever takes this role.

We will consider visa sponsorship, but will prioritize candidates who already have the legal right to work in Hong Kong.

If you don't have that formal background, we still want to hear from you. In that case, expect to show demonstrable taste and creativity through the hiring process.

About the principal

A European-Hong Kong family. Wealth created through technology entrepreneurship and private equity. Engaged in a great deal of philanthropic work, which is handled separately within the family office and sits outside this role.

The principal works hard, weekdays and weekends. The off-hours are for the people he loves: his wife, his family, his closest friends. He sees life as short, and the time off as the moments worth maximizing, with as much beauty and meaning packed in as possible.

Privacy, judgement, reliability, creativity, and taste are the five things he values most in a role like this.

The principal runs a small, lean team that leans heavily on AI. The Experience Manager is expected to learn to leverage AI heavily, using the tools fluently to plan faster, search smarter, brief vendors better, and operate at a higher pace than a traditional EA or events lead could.

Terms

Compensation

HKD 50,000 / month base, discretionary bonus

Benefits

Medical insurance, MPF, 18 days annual leave

Travel

Up to 30 days a year, mostly to places people save for their honeymoon.

Location

Hong Kong. The family office is in Central.

Working pattern

Flexible. Work from home when you are not needed in person. The office in Central is yours when you want it.

snippet: Legal, compliance, and asset management in one—oversee portfolios, handle disclosures, and execute asset disposals.
label: 法律辅助
full_jd:
Job Responsibilities Description

Deeply participate in the management of post-investment projects related to Hong Kong-listed companies, including asset monitoring, compliance supervision, and value analysis.​

Assist in or be responsible for handling legal, compliance, and information disclosure matters related to the managed assets in the Hong Kong capital market, maintaining communication with regulatory bodies, listed companies, and other relevant parties.​

Track and research the rules, regulatory trends, and market dynamics of the Hong Kong capital market to support post-investment management decisions.​

Be responsible for or lead the disposal of various assets in existing projects, including but not limited to real estate, land, equity, etc., and formulate and execute asset disposal plans.​

Fully responsible for reviewing, drafting, and negotiating various commercial contracts and legal documents to ensure they are legally sound, effective, and protect the company’s interests.

Job Qualification Requirements

Bachelor’s degree or above in Law, Finance, Economics, Accounting, or related disciplines. A legal background is preferred.

3-5 years of relevant work experience in asset management, investment banking, law firms, or listed companies.

Familiar with the operational rules, regulatory requirements, and information disclosure systems of the Hong Kong capital market.

Practical experience in the disposal of complex assets, such as real estate, equity, or other investment portfolios.

Excellent command of both written and spoken Chinese and English, with the ability to handle professional business and legal documents.

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, negotiation and coordination abilities, and a high level of resilience under pressure.

Previous experience in a Hong Kong listed company as a Board Secretary or in the legal function is preferred; an SOE background is highly advantageous.
